### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications across the files are interconnected through the introduction and utilization of the `scmi_reset_rx_to_maxsz` function. This function is defined in `driver.c` and is called in multiple files (`sensors.c`, `clock.c`, `perf.c`, and `base.c`) to ensure that the receive buffer size is reset to the maximum possible size whenever a new command is processed. This is crucial for handling cases where multiple commands may be sent consecutively, and the response size may vary, preventing incorrect interpretation of the response size. The changes collectively enhance the robustness of the firmware's handling of SCMI (System Control and Management Interface) commands.

Here is the commit message:
firmware: arm_scmi: Add missing Rx size re-initialisation

Few commands provide the list of description partially and require
to be called consecutively until all the descriptors are fetched
completely. In such cases, we don't release the buffers and reuse
them for consecutive transmits.

However, currently we don't reset the Rx size which will be set as
per the response for the last transmit. This may result in incorrect
response size being interpretted as the firmware may repond with size
greater than the one set but we read only upto the size set by previous
response.

Let us reset the receive buffer size to max possible in such cases as
we don't know the exact size of the response.

Link:  https://lore.kernel.org/r/20201012141746.32575-1-sudeep.holla@arm.com
Fixes: b6f20ff8bd94 ("firmware: arm_scmi: add common infrastructure and support for base protocol")
Reported-by: Etienne Carriere <etienne.carriere@linaro.org>
Signed-off-by: Sudeep Holla <sudeep.holla@arm.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the failure to reset the receive buffer size after processing commands that may return multiple responses. This can lead to incorrect interpretation of response sizes, as the buffer retains the size set by the previous response, potentially causing the system to read only a portion of a larger response from the firmware.

Here is the patch:
 
+void scmi_reset_rx_to_maxsz(const struct scmi_handle *handle,
+			    struct scmi_xfer *xfer)
+{
+	struct scmi_info *info = handle_to_scmi_info(handle);
+
+	xfer->rx.len = info->desc->max_msg_size;
+}
+
 #define SCMI_MAX_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT	(2 * MSEC_PER_SEC)

Reason:
The bug occurs because the receive buffer size (`xfer->rx.len`) is not reset after processing commands that may return multiple responses. This means that if the previous response size was smaller than the actual size of the next response, the system will only read up to the previous size, leading to incomplete data being interpreted.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
xfer->rx.len = info->desc->max_msg_size;
```
```c
scmi_reset_rx_to_maxsz(handle, xfer);
```
Reason:
The fix involves resetting the receive buffer size to the maximum possible size (`info->desc->max_msg_size`) before processing the next command. This ensures that the system is prepared to handle the full response size from the firmware, preventing any misinterpretation of the response data.
